lines.text: Lines forty-seven and forty-eight: limit takes current, wanted and d t. Each velocity holds v x, v y and omega, along the field.
In goes our example. Current: three point six, zero, one. Wanted: four, zero, three. d t: zero point zero two.
Line forty-nine: a x, the change in v x over d t. Twenty.
Line fifty: a y. Zero, since we drive straight along x.
Lines fifty-one and fifty-two: alpha, the change in omega over d t, clamped between minus eight and eight. One hundred becomes eight. Check one.
Lines fifty-four and fifty-five are comments: only speeding up is limited, and spin-up isn't counted.
Line fifty-six asks: are we speeding up? It's a dot product: multiply x with x, y with y, and add.
Positive means speeding up. Twenty times three point six is seventy-two, so we check the motors.
Lines fifty-seven and fifty-eight: wheel speed, the fastest any wheel could move. Speed, plus spin times base radius: three point nine six.
Line fifty-nine: motor accel at that speed. Motor limit is ten point four nine.
Line sixty: a, the size of the driving acceleration. Hypot, short for hypotenuse, is Pythagoras in one call. Twenty.
Lines sixty-one to sixty-four: if a is too big, scale a x and a y by motor limit over a. Twenty becomes ten point four nine.
Alpha isn't cut here: in our simulator, cutting spin-up too, like the twenty twenty-six code, slowed turns while driving.
